# TÀI Studio — User guide
# TÀI Studio — Agent Overview
This page provides a comprehensive overview of all agents in the TÀI Studio ecosystem.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Agent Index
| # | Name | Description | Availability |
| 1 | The Translator | Translate documents between languages preserving formatting | Ready |
| 2 | The Summarizer | Summarize uploaded documents | Ready |
| 3 | The Powerpoint-er | Generate branded PPTX presentations | Ready |
| 4 | The Brainstormer | Structured brainstorming with canvas | Ready |
| 5 | TÀI (Super Agent) | Unified AI assistant with LangGraph tool calling to all specialist agents | Ready |
| 6 | The AI Visionary | AI vision Q&A + PPTX reports | Ready |

──────────────────────────────────────────────────
# What do you need to do? → Pick the right agent
The Agent Platform provides two types of agents designed to support different working styles and needs:
- Super Agent – a general-purpose assistant that understands requests and orchestrates tasks across multiple agents.
- Featured Agents – specialized tools built to complete a single task quickly and efficiently (Summarizer, Translator, Powerpoint-er)
Understanding when to use each type will help you achieve the best results.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## 1. Super Agent - TÀI (Central Assistant)
The Super Agent acts as your primary entry point. It interacts conversationally and determines how to fulfill your request, including calling other agents when necessary.
### Key Capabilities
- Interprets natural language requests
- Breaks down complex tasks into steps
- Coordinates multiple actions in one workflow
- Provides guidance and suggestions when needed
### When to Use
Use the Super Agent in the following situations:
- You are unsure which agent is appropriate
- Your request involves multiple steps or tasks
- You need clarification, brainstorming, or iterative refinement
- You want a single interaction to manage an end-to-end process
### Input / Output
- Input: Text, optionally with attached files
- Output: Text responses, processed files, or aggregated results
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## 2. Featured Agents (Task-Focused Tools)
Featured Agents are optimized for individual tasks. They operate with higher speed and consistency when the objective is clearly defined.
### Available Agents
- Summarizer – Extracts key insights and produces concise summaries
- Translator – Translates documents while preserving original format
- PowerPoint-er – Generates and customizes presentation slides
- AI Visionary – QnA about Techcomabank Vision & Goal
- Brainstormer – Building ideas/solution step by step
### Key Characteristics
- Focused on one function
- Faster execution due to minimal orchestration
- Direct interaction with files and structured inputs
### When to Use
Use a Featured Agent in the following situations:
- You know exactly what task you want to complete
- You already have the required input (files or text)
- You need fast and predictable output
- You do not require additional guidance or multi-step processing
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## 3. Choosing the Right Agent
Use the following guidance to select the appropriate starting point:
- Start with the Super Agent if:
- The request is unclear or exploratory
- The task involves multiple outputs (e.g., summarize and translate)
- You prefer guided interaction
- Use a Featured Agent if:
- The task is clearly defined
- Speed and efficiency are priorities
- You want direct control over input and output
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## 4. Example Use Cases
| Scenario | Recommended Agent |
| “Summarize this report and create slides from it” | Super Agent |
| “Translate this PDF into English” | Translator |
| “Create a presentation from this outline” | PowerPoint-er |
| “Summarize multiple documents quickly” | Summarizer |
| “I need help deciding what to do with my data” | Super Agent |
| “Lets build idea for new product” | Brainstormer |
| “What are Techcombank goal & objective?” | AI Visionary/Super Agent |

──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## 5. Best Practice
- Start with the Super Agent when in doubt. You can always transition to a Featured Agent.
- Use Featured Agents for repetitive or standardized tasks.
- Provide clear inputs (especially files and context) to improve output quality.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────

# User Guide — Office 365 Connector
## Overview
The Office 365 Connector is an MCP (Model Context Protocol) connection that allows the TÀI AI assistant to access your Microsoft 365 directly — including Outlook Mail, Outlook Calendar, and Microsoft Teams — right within the TÀI Studio chat interface.
Key differentiators of the Office 365 Connector:
- Quick access: read emails, calendar events, and Teams messages without leaving TÀI Studio.
- Personal security: always operates under your own account and permissions — no shared or admin accounts are used.
- Read-only (MVP 1): currently supports viewing information only, cannot send emails or create events — ensuring complete safety.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Activation & Login
To use the Office 365 Connector, you need to activate it in TÀI Studio:
- In the message input area, click the "+" button (bottom-left corner).
- The "Search connectors" popup appears with tabs: All, Agents, and MCPs.
- Under the MCPs section, check Office 365.
Note: Agents (The Powerpoint-er, My AI Coach, The Imaginator…) and MCPs are two separate types of connectors. Office 365 is in the MCPs group.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Automatic Authentication
As soon as you check Office 365, the system will automatically authenticate your Microsoft 365 account:
- After selecting Office 365 in the connector popup, the system automatically connects to your Techcombank account (@techcombank.com.vn).
- The screen displays a "Login successful" message along with the authenticated account email.
- The popup closes automatically after 2 seconds — you can start using it immediately.
No password entry or login links required — the process is fully automatic based on your current login session.
Session duration:
- Access token auto-refreshes within 1 hour.
- Total session lasts 7 days — after that, you need to reactivate the connector to re-authenticate.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Main Features
The Office 365 Connector supports 3 feature groups: Mail, Calendar, and Teams.
### Outlook Mail — Read Emails
You can ask TÀI to:
| Request | Example prompt |
| View latest emails | "List my 5 most recent emails" |
| Find emails by sender | "Find emails from nguyenva@techcombank.com.vn" |
| Find emails by subject | "Find emails with subject containing 'meeting'" |
| Read email details | "Read the details of the first email in the list" |
| View emails with attachments | "Find emails with attachments" |
| View emails in folder | "List emails in the drafts folder" |

Information displayed:
- Email list: date received, sender, subject, read/unread status, content preview (200 characters).
- Email details: full content, recipient list (to, cc), attachment information.
Note: Cannot download attachment content — only the name, type, and size are visible.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
### Outlook Calendar — View Meetings
You can ask TÀI to:
| Request | Example prompt |
| View upcoming meetings | "What meetings do I have this week?" |
| View meeting details | "Details of the first meeting in the list" |
| Find free time slots | "Find 2 free hours tomorrow" |
| View calendar list | "What calendars do I have?" |

Information displayed:
- Meeting list: title, start/end time, location, organizer, meeting type (online/offline).
- Meeting details: attendee list, agenda, join link (for online meetings).
- Free time search: available time slots with suggested notes.
Note: Free time search only provides suggestions — it does not automatically schedule meetings. Results are displayed in Vietnam time (Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh).
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
### Microsoft Teams — Read Messages
You can ask TÀI to:
| Request | Example prompt |
| View team list | "What teams am I part of?" |
| View channels in a team | "What channels does team XYZ have?" |
| Read channel messages | "Read the 5 latest messages in the General channel" |
| View conversations | "List recent Teams conversations" |
| Read chat messages | "Read messages in the first conversation" |

Information displayed:
- Conversation list: type (Meeting / Group / 1:1) and name/topic.
- Messages: sender, time, content (truncated at 200 characters).
Note: 1-on-1 chats often do not display participant names — TÀI will indicate when it cannot determine who the conversation is with.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
### Search Colleagues
You can ask TÀI to find colleague information by name:
| Request | Example prompt |
| Find colleague information | "Find user Thuc Nguyen Minh" |

Information displayed:
- Full name, email, job title, department.
- If multiple results match, TÀI will ask you to select the correct person.
- If no results found, try searching with a single word from the name (first or last name only).
Note: Only people you have previously interacted with can be found — not the entire company directory.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Logging Out of Office 365
When you want to disconnect Office 365 from TÀI Studio:
- Type "logout o365" (or similar commands like "log out of Office 365") in the chat input.
- TÀI will perform the logout and confirm: "You've been logged out of Office 365. Your cached credentials have been cleared."
When to log out:
- When you want to stop TÀI from accessing your Microsoft 365.
- When you want to switch to a different account.
- For security reasons — for example, when using a shared device.
After logging out, you need to reactivate the Office 365 connector (check it again in the "+" popup) to authenticate and continue using it.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## How TÀI Processes Office 365 Requests
When you send a question related to Office 365, TÀI performs these steps:
- Check connection — confirm the session is still valid.
- Select the appropriate tool — automatically choose the right tool based on your question (e.g., list_mail_messages, get_calendar_view).
- Call Microsoft Graph API — query data from your Microsoft 365.
- Present results — display information in an easy-to-read table or list format.
You may see an "Office 365 ✓" label in the response — this confirms TÀI successfully used the connector.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Security & Access
The Office 365 Connector is designed with multiple security layers:
| Security Layer | Details |
| Automatic authentication | Identity verified via SSO — no password re-entry needed |
| Permissions | Uses only your own permissions (delegated) — no admin access |
| Read-only | MVP 1 supports reading only — cannot send emails, create/edit/delete meetings |
| Encryption | Tokens encrypted with AES-256-GCM, isolated per user |
| No content storage | Email/chat content is not stored — Microsoft 365 is the sole source |
| Proactive logout | Users can logout at any time to clear cached credentials |
| Audit | Every tool call generates an audit log entry |

──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Tips
- Be as specific as possible — "List my 5 latest emails" gets faster results than "Check my mail".
- Specify quantities when needed (e.g., "5 emails", "3 meetings this week").
- Specify time ranges when asking about calendar (e.g., "from 18/08 to 22/08/2026").
- Use real names when searching for colleagues — full email address is not required.
- When TÀI asks for clarification (e.g., "Whose email do you mean?"), reply specifically — TÀI does not guess.
- Combine multiple requests in one message (e.g., "Check new emails and tomorrow's meetings").
- Type "logout o365" when you want to disconnect.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Limitations
| Limitation | Details |
| Read-only | Cannot send emails, create/edit/delete meetings, or send Teams messages |
| No attachment download | Only name, type, and size of attachments are visible — content cannot be downloaded |
| No transcript viewing | Meeting transcript reading is not yet enabled |
| Limited preview | Email and message content in lists is truncated at 200 characters — request details for full content |
| Limited people search | Only finds people you have previously interacted with, not the entire directory |
| Session expiry | After 7 days, you need to reactivate the connector to re-authenticate |
| Incomplete results | If TÀI says "hasMore: true", there is more data available — you can ask to see more |

──────────────────────────────────────────────────
This guide applies to the Office 365 Connector (MVP 1 — read-only).
⚠️ Responses may not always be accurate — please verify important information.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
Last updated: 18/08/2026

pages.markdown:
# User Guide — AI Coach
## Overview
AI Coach is an AI learning assistant that personalizes content and learning paths based on your level, learning style, and goals — from your first steps exploring AI all the way to earning a professional certification and applying AI to real work.
What sets AI Coach apart:
- Understands you: remembers your level, role, preferences, and goals so every answer is pitched at the right level.
- Has a roadmap: builds and tracks a personal learning path, rather than just answering isolated questions.
- Tied to your work: helps you shape a real work situation into a safe, compliant AI use case.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Interface layout
The interface has a left navigation bar (sidebar) and a main content area on the right.
The left sidebar is split into 2 groups:
| Group | Item | Function |
| WORKSPACE | Today | Daily home — what to do next, a short daily mission, and an overall progress snapshot |
|  | My Journey | Your active personal learning path |
|  | Build | Shape a real work situation into a safe AI use case |
|  | Explore | Discover AI tools and certifications |
|  | Progress | Track your growth with evidence |
| ASSISTANT | Open Coach | Open a direct chat with AI Coach |

The top bar (shown on every page):
- Breadcrumb — your current location (e.g. AI Coach / Coach).
- History — review your past conversations.
- Ask AI Coach — quickly open a chat from any page.
The bottom-left corner shows your profile: your name and current level (e.g. "Competent user"). It's a shortcut to view/edit your learning profile.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## First-time setup
On your first visit, you go through 3 quick setup steps ("Personalize your AI Coach"). Each answer helps Coach tune content to your exact level, role, and language.
### Step 1 — Your level
Choose 1 of 5 AI levels (from Beginner to Revolution leader). All content and recommendations in the app are personalized to the level you choose.
### Step 2 — How you learn
Choose how you learn best:
- Hands-on — learn by doing, through labs and real examples.
- Conceptual — understand the essence first; the "why" comes first.
- Goal-driven — learn toward a goal, the shortest path to results.
- Social — learn with others, through cohorts, mentors, and community.
Then choose your preferred response language: Vietnamese or English.
### Step 3 — Role & goals
- Your role: information from your HR profile is pre-filled (full name, position, department, division). If it's not right, click "No — edit my details" to adjust.
- Which skills do you want to develop?: select as many as you like — GenAI & Prompting, AI for Office (M365 Copilot), Coding with AI, BI / Analytics, Data Engineering, AI Agents & Automation, AI Governance & Risk.
- Learning goal (optional): enter a specific learning goal (e.g. "in 3 months, build a Q&A dashboard with Genie on my own").
Click Finish to complete setup and enter the Today page.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Today — Daily home
Today is your starting point each day, summarizing what to do and your learning status on a single page:
- Do this next — what to do next, suggesting your immediate next action in the roadmap.
- Today's mission — a short task (about 10 minutes) to keep your learning habit going.
- Check-in panel ("On track" / "Nothing owed") — whether you're keeping up with your roadmap, along with metrics like roadmap progress and the number of Level Checks passed.
- Journey progress — a doughnut chart showing your roadmap completion percentage.
- Recommended next — suggestions for the next step: continue the roadmap or take a Level Check.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Open Coach — Chat with AI Coach
This is where you ask questions, learn, and ask Coach to build a roadmap.
Chat list (left of the Coach panel): a New chat button to start a new conversation, plus a Recent list of saved conversations (reopen any of them anytime).
Coach voice: just above the input box there's a menu to pick the response style that fits your needs:
| Voice | When to use |
| Default | Coach picks a suitable voice automatically |
| Mentor | Gentle, step-by-step support |
| Peer | Like a teammate learning alongside you, casual |
| Instructor | Structured, teaches with checks |
| Exam coach | Drills recall to prepare for a Level Check |
| Concise expert | Brief, assumes you already have the fundamentals |
| Delivery partner | Helps scope the real problem and plan the rollout |
| Socratic | Asks probing questions so you spot the gaps yourself |
| Risk drill | Role-plays a use case and identifies its risk zones |

Mention a specific tool: type @ in the input box to direct your question at a specific AI tool (e.g. @TÀI Studio).
Note: Coach may answer inaccurately — always verify important information. Your profile is used to personalize answers.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## My Journey — Personal learning path
This page shows your active learning path and lets you track and edit your progress.
Main components:
- Active roadmap — the path you're following, with the number of completed nodes ("X / Y complete") and a percentage progress bar.
- Action buttons at the top:
- Review with Coach — ask Coach to review your path and suggest adjustments (opens Coach with a prepared question).
- New journey — create a new learning path.
- Right column:
- Active certification goal — the certification you're targeting (links to Explore).
- Open commitments — commitments/tasks still in progress.
View mode: the path shows in Classic view by default (the familiar phase map). You can change the view using the toggle at the top of the path if you want a different layout.
Update each node's progress: each node has 4 states, switched quickly with keyboard shortcuts:
| Key | State | Meaning |
| T | Not started | Not started yet |
| L | In progress | Currently learning |
| D | Done | Completed |
| S | Skipped |

When you mark a node "Done", the path's completion percentage increases accordingly.
When you click a node/topic: a detail panel opens with these actions:
- Learn this now — start learning the topic right away.
- Explain — Coach explains more about the topic.
- Test my Knowledge — check your level of understanding.
- Remove from roadmap — remove the topic from the path if it doesn't fit.
- Includes the recommended course for the topic (course name, source) when available.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Build — Shape a safe use case
Build helps you turn a real work situation into a clearly shaped, compliant AI use case. The page has 2 states.
### State 1 — Describe the work
The screen asks "What work would you like to improve?" with an input box and a Shape this use case button. Quick suggestions are available to get started:
- Prepare for a meeting
- Analyse recurring work
- Draft a document
When you click Shape this use case (or pick a suggestion), Build moves your request into a chat with Coach. Coach asks a few short questions to clarify the context and governance factors (e.g. what type of work it is, what exactly you need to produce), then helps shape the use case and suggests suitable AI tools.
### State 2 — Shape a safe solution
After talking with Coach, the Build page becomes "Shape a safe solution" — a draft solution tied to the risk zone the system classifies:
- Draft solution — a draft use case with a risk-zone label (e.g. Green zone) and a status ("Coach is still gathering information for the brief").
- Solution shape — a sequence of steps: Data → Tool → Output → Human review, each with a status to confirm ("To confirm" / "Before use"), plus a Review link.
- Next steps — next steps are sketched out progressively as you keep chatting.
- Safe-scope simulator (What-if) — a simulation tool: change the choices to see how the risk zone shifts (using the exact classifier Coach uses). The criteria include:
- What it produces — what the output is (e.g. a human-reviewed draft).
- Data it uses — which data is used (e.g. internal data only).
- A customer sees the result — whether a customer sees the result.
- Who relies on it — who depends on this result.
- The simulation shows a tier label (e.g. tier T2) and warnings that need clarification. This is only a trial ("preliminary — not an approval") — it is not an approval and is not saved or sent anywhere.
- Continue with Coach — go back to the chat to keep refining.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Explore — AI Tools & Certifications
The Explore page has a toggle between AI Tools and Certifications (top right), plus an All / Unlocked for me filter (shows only items unlocked for you).
### AI Tools
The list of AI tools available at Techcombank. Each tool card shows:
- The required level and locked/unlocked status.
- Tier (e.g. T2 / T3) and the tool group/category.
- Action buttons:
- Ask Coach — if the tool is unlocked, ask Coach for details on how to use it.
- Level check — if the tool is locked, take a check to reach the unlocking level.
### Certifications
The list of certifications from Microsoft, Databricks, Google Cloud, AWS. Each card shows:
- The provider and the certification's level.
- Hint labels such as "Fits your level" / "Recommended".
- Action buttons:
- Set goal — set the certification as a goal (attached to My Journey).
- Prep — create a review path for that certification.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Progress — Learning progress
The Progress page ("Your growth, with evidence.") gives you an overview of your growth, with concrete evidence:
- Current level card — e.g. "L2 · Competent user", with your roadmap completion percentage and a Take level check button.
- Learning momentum — a chart showing your learning pace over time (it measures activity, not scores).
- What the coach has learned — things Coach has recorded about you, shown as labeled cards (INTEREST / PREFERENCE). Each card has a "Not accurate — forget this" button to ask Coach to forget incorrect information.
- Close your gaps — where you're weak: the number of questions answered incorrectly, with suggestions to "complete the current roadmap phase" and "review the ones you got wrong".
- Why these recommendations — a transparent explanation of why these recommendations appear.
- Edit learning profile — edit your learning profile.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Level system
AI Coach has 5 skill levels:
| Level | Name | Short description |
| 1 | Beginner | Understand AI basics, recognize applications, comply with policies |
| 2 | Competent user | Use AI tools, interpret results to make decisions |
| 3 | Expert | Design AI use cases, collaborate with technical teams |
| 4 | Technical Professional | Develop & deploy AI models, manage the model lifecycle |
| 5 | Revolution leader | Shape AI strategy, train teams across the organization |

AI Coach recommends tools and content suited to your current level. If a topic is above your level, Coach lists the prerequisite knowledge and suggests a path to reach that content.
### How to level up
- Your level rises through learning and practice: answering practice questions correctly, completing roadmaps, and continuous engagement.
- When you're ready, take a Level Check to officially level up. You can open a Level Check from several places: the Progress page, the Today page, or the welcome card in Open Coach.
|  | Level Check (scored) | Practice Quiz (practice) |
| Questions | 6 | Optional |
| Pass | ≥70% → level up by 1 | No effect on level |
| Fail | Locked for 4 hours | Retry immediately |

──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Tips
- Describe your request as specifically as possible — "Explain RAG architecture" gives better results than "Explain AI".
- Pick the Coach voice that fits your purpose: Exam coach when studying for a Level Check, Delivery partner when planning a rollout, Concise expert when you need a brief answer.
- Type @ in the chat box to ask about a specific tool (e.g. @TÀI Studio).
- Use Build when you have a real task to improve — Coach will shape the use case and check the risk zone before you use it for real.
- Go to Progress → Close your gaps to review the questions you answered incorrectly.
- If Coach records something incorrect about you, use "Not accurate — forget this" in Progress to correct it.
- Practice regularly — level-up progress accumulates from every interaction.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Limitations
- AI Coach only supports content related to AI and technology at Techcombank.
- It does not provide medical, legal, or personal financial advice.
- The Safe-scope simulator results are preliminary reference only, not an official risk approval.
- Answers may be inaccurate — always verify important information.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
Last updated at: 23/07/2026

# User Guide — The AI Visionary
# The AI Visionary — User Guide
## Overview
The AI Visionary is a knowledge support tool designed to provide insights into Techcombank’s AI strategy, vision, and roadmap across various divisions. All information presented is sourced from official Techcombank documents, ensuring accuracy and reliability.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Interface Layout
| Area | Purpose |
| Main area | Main area is chat-based conversation, where users can interact with the AI to ask questions about Techcombank’s internal information |

──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## How to Use
### AI Vision Q&A
Simply type your question about AI strategy, vision, or technology trends. The AI responds with detailed, informed answers.
Example questions (hint chips):
- "What is Techcombank AI vision?"
- "How can GenAI improve operations?"
- "AI roadmap priorities for banking"
Press Enter to send. The AI responds with markdown-formatted answers.
### How the AI Works
The AI analyzes all available internal data sources provided to it and identifies relevant information related to the user’s query. Based on this analysis, it generates a comprehensive answer.
At the end of each response, the AI includes a list of sources it referenced, enabling users to track and validate the information.
User can download the resource by press on them.
### AI Vision Feedback
Users can provide feedback via the feedback button located at the bottom right corner. This includes sharing opinions, suggestions, or reporting issues.
Collecting more feedback enables deeper insights, helping continuously improve and enhance TÀI Studio.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Tips
- Ask clear, specific questions to get better answers
- Use example questions (hint chips) as a quick starting point
- Check the listed sources for more details and validation
- Works well for weekly summary decks, strategy presentations, and AI roadmap updates
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Limitations
- Presentations use text only — no embedded images
- Quality depends on the specificity of your request
- The AI's knowledge is focused on AI/technology strategy topics
- Answers depend on available internal documents only
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
Last updated: 2026-06-22

# User Guide — The Brainstormer
# The Brainstormer — User Guide
## Overview
The Brainstormer is a structured thinking partner that helps you explore ideas, clarify problems, and converge on solutions. It features a chat interface paired with a live "Thinking Canvas" that organizes your brainstorming session into actionable components.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Interface Layout
The page is divided into 2 panels:
| Panel | Purpose |
| Left (58%) | Chat conversation with the AI |
| Right (42%) | Thinking Canvas — structured output |

──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## How to Use
### Step 1: Start a Conversation
Type your idea, problem, or question in the input bar at the bottom. You can also click one of the hint chips for inspiration: - "New product idea" - "Architecture decision" - "Prioritize between options" - "Vague idea I want to explore"
Press Enter to send (Shift+Enter for new line).
### Step 2: Engage in Dialogue
The Brainstormer will ask clarifying questions and guide you through structured thinking. Respond naturally — even rough thoughts work perfectly. The AI adapts to your communication style.
Note:
- At the top of the conversation, click on the current flow to open a dropdown menu displaying available thinking workflows.
- Select a different workflow to adjust how the AI structures its reasoning and responses.
- Any new questions will follow the newly selected workflow.
- Workflows can be switched at any time during the conversation, providing flexibility in how insights are generated.
### Step 3: Watch the Canvas Build
As the conversation progresses, the Thinking Canvas on the right automatically populates with:
| Section | Content |
| Core Problem | The refined problem statement |
| Ideas | List of approaches focused on user intent and goals |
| Options Explored | List of alternatives considered |
| Action Plan | Concrete next steps |

Each section fills in as the AI identifies relevant content from your conversation.
### Step 4: Session Completion
When the brainstorming reaches a natural conclusion, the session is marked as complete:
- A green "✓ Session complete — canvas is ready" message appears
- The input bar is replaced with a "New session" button
- Your canvas contains the final structured output
### Output export
At the top-right corner, there are 2 output options:
- Copy Output Content: Copies the full response while preserving its Markdown formatting for easy reuse.
- Export Brainstorming Workflow: Exports the AI-generated ideas and structure into an .xmind file format for mind mapping and further refinement.
### Starting Fresh
Click "New session" in the chat header (or after completion) to start a new brainstorming session with a clean canvas.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Features
- Cross-session memory — The Brainstormer remembers your preferences (language, tone, preferred topics) across sessions
- Structured output — Every session produces an organized canvas, not just chat history
- Guided exploration — The AI asks the right questions to help you think deeper
- Session tracking — See exchange count in the header
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Tips
- Start with a rough idea — the AI will help you refine it
- Be honest about uncertainty — "I'm not sure what I want" is a valid starting point
- The canvas is the deliverable — use it to share your thinking with others
- Multiple short sessions often work better than one long one
- The AI adapts to your language preference over time
- Change the conversation flow anytime during the chat to find the most suitable reasoning style.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Limitations
- Long-term memory stores preferences only (language, tone, topics), not full chat history
- Each session is independent — the AI doesn't recall previous session content
- Best suited for strategic thinking, not detailed implementation planning
- No file upload support — text-based interaction only
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
Last updated: 2026-06-22

# User Guide — The Imaginator
# The Imaginator — User Guide
## Overview
The Imaginator generates high-quality AI images from text descriptions (text-to-image) or from a combination of text and reference images (image-to-image) on a single canvas. It supports a variety of built-in styles, customizable aspect ratios and resolutions, and lets you produce up to 4 variations per generation.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Supported input formats
- PNG (.png)
- JPG / JPEG (.jpg, .jpeg)
Maximum file size: 10 MB per reference image
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Interface layout
The page is divided into 3 panels:
| Panel | Purpose |
| Left (Node Panel) | Drag and drop nodes (Prompt, Image Input, Generate, Output) and control the canvas (Undo/Redo/Reset) |
| Center (Canvas) | Workspace — connect nodes to build your image-generation pipeline |
| Right (History) | Shows the history of recently generated images |

──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## How to use
When you open The Imaginator, the default view shows a canvas with three pre-connected nodes: Prompt → Generate → Output.
### Step 1: Describe the image
In the Prompt node, enter a description of the image you want to create. You can:
- Type the description directly
- Pick a style from the dropdown below the node
- Click “Enhance” to let AI automatically enrich your description
If you want to use an image as a reference, drag the Image Input node from the left panel onto the canvas, upload an image (PNG/JPG, up to 10 MB), then connect it to the Generate node.
### Step 2: Configure generation settings
In the Generate node, configure the following options:
- Aspect ratio / Size — Defaults to 1:1 · 1024×1024; click to change the aspect ratio and resolution
- Format — WebP (default) or PNG
- Number of variations — From 1 to 4
### Step 3: Generate the image
Click the red “Generate” button at the bottom of the Generate node and wait for processing.
### Step 4: Review and interact with the result
Once complete, the image appears in the Output node with the following actions:
- Text — Add text on top of the image
- Edit — Refine the image with AI
- View — Open the image in full-screen view
- Save — Download the image to your device
- Compare — Compare outputs using a slider
- Input — Use this image as the input for the next generation
- Keep — When you have multiple results, keep the best one
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Tips
- The more detailed the description, the better — specify the subject, setting, lighting, and camera angle for more accurate results
- Use “Enhance” when your prompt is short or generic — the AI will automatically fill in the details
- Start with the Fast (1K) resolution for experimentation, then switch to Ultra HD (4K) for the final version
- Generate multiple variations (2–4) to have more options, then use Keep to save the best one
- Use the Input button on the Output node to iterate — turn a just-generated image into a reference for the next round
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Limitations
- Maximum upload size: 10 MB per file
- Input image formats are limited to PNG and JPG
- Maximum variations per generation: 4
- Content that violates safety policies will be blocked automatically
──────────────────────────────────────────────────

# User Guide — The Powerpoint-er
# The Powerpoint-er — User Guide
## Overview
The Powerpoint-er generates branded PPTX presentations from text descriptions. It uses a 3-step pipeline: describe your content → review/edit the outline → preview and export slides. The entire export happens in your browser — no server-side rendering needed.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## How to Use
### Step 1: Write Your Brief
On the left panel, describe the presentation you want. Be specific about: - Topic and audience - Number of slides desired - Key points to cover - Tone (formal, casual, executive)
You can also upload reference files to provide context.
Example prompts:
- "Create a 10-slide deck on AI strategy 2025 for the executive board"
- "Build a quarterly business review with revenue, customer growth, and roadmap"
- "Make a 5-slide onboarding presentation for new engineers"
### Step 2: Review the Outline
After the AI generates an outline, you'll see an editable slide panel showing: - Cover slide - Content slides with titles and bullet points - Closing slide
You can edit: - Slide titles (click to edit) - Bullet points (click to edit) - Add/remove bullets (+ Add bullet / × to remove) - Add/remove slides (+ Add slide / Remove) - Reorder content as needed (­Up / Down arrows at the upper right)
### Step 3: Build & Preview
Click "Build Presentation" to generate the full slide HTML. Each slide is rendered as a visual preview that you can:
- Browse through using navigation
- View in a presentation mode
- Edit the outline and rebuild if needed
### Step 4: Slide Edition
- The top bar provides quick editing actions, including adjusting font size, text color, formatting, alignment, and adding bullet points to the content.
- The “Ask AI to edit” field allows a short description of the desired changes. This helps guide AI to update the content more accurately.
- Click “Save” to apply the edit or “Cancel” to discard changes
- If changes have been saved but the original output is needed again, click “Regenerate from outline” to restore the initial generated version.
### Step 5: Export
Choose your export format:
- PPTX — Native PowerPoint file with editable text, vector graphics, and speaker notes
- PDF — Image-based PDF (visual fidelity, text not selectable)
The export runs entirely in your browser. A progress overlay shows the export status.
The homepage of PowerPoint-er displays all previously saved presentations, click “Open” to see fully.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Features
- Branded templates — Slides use Techcombank's visual identity
- Speaker notes — AI generates notes for each slide, injected into the PPTX
- Editable output — PPTX contains native shapes and text (not images)
- Browser-side export — No server round-trip for the final file
- Live preview — See exactly how slides will look before exporting
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Tips
- Be specific in your brief — the more detail you provide, the better the output
- Edit the outline before building — it's much faster than regenerating
- Use the speaker notes for presentation preparation
- For complex presentations, break them into sections and describe each
- The AI handles Vietnamese and English content equally well
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Limitations
- Layouts depend on bundled templates — no custom animations or complex charts
- Very long presentations (30+ slides) may take longer to generate
- Image insertion is not supported — slides contain text and vector graphics only
- Adding templates directly is not available; full requirements must be clearly described in text
- During slide editing, only inline content updates are supported. Adding new text boxes or repositioning existing elements is not available
- For advanced adjustments, required export and download the PowerPoint file for local editing
- Export requires a modern browser (Chrome, Edge, Firefox)
──────────────────────────────────────────────────

# User Guide — The Scholar
# The Scholar — User Guide
## Overview
The Scholar is a personal research assistant that helps you organize documents into notebooks, ask questions and receive answers with precise citations from your provided sources, along with a Studio toolkit that transforms documents into reports, mind maps, flashcards, quizzes, and more — without fabricating information beyond the sources.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Interface Layout
3-column interface: Sources (left) · Chat (center) · Studio (right)
When entering a notebook, the screen is divided into 3 areas:
| Area | Purpose |
| Left (Sources) | List of sources added to the notebook; add source button (Upload file / Paste text); select/deselect sources to limit answer scope |
| Center (Chat) | Question input field, initial quick suggestions, cited answers with clickable references, and follow-up suggestions |
| Right (Studio) | 6 tools to generate outputs from sources (Report, Mind Map, Flashcards, Quiz, Data Table, Infographic) + Notes |

Before entering a notebook, you’ll see the Hub — an overview page showing all your notebooks and notebooks shared with you.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## How to Use
### Step 1: Create a Notebook
From the Hub, click Create Notebook. Each notebook is a separate research space — sources in one notebook are completely isolated from others.
You can choose a pre-made template or start with a blank notebook: - Literature review - Study guide - Meeting notes - Blank
### Step 2: Add Sources
Sources panel with status indicators: green dot (ready) and yellow dot (processing)
There are 2 ways to add sources:
| Method | Description |
| Upload file | Select a file from your computer. Supported: PDF, DOCX, PPTX, TXT, MD, JPG, PNG — max 20 MB per file |
| Paste text | Copy-paste content directly — max 480,000 characters |

After adding, a source will be in Processing state (yellow dot) → the system analyzes, chunks, and indexes it. When complete, it changes to Ready (green dot). If there’s an error → Unreadable (red dot), you can retry processing.
### Step 3: Chat
Answer with citations [1][2] and 3 follow-up suggestions
Ask questions about your documents. The Scholar will: - Search within selected sources - Answer with citations [1], [2], … — click a citation to view the original passage - Suggest 3 follow-up questions
### Step 4: Use Studio to Generate Outputs
Select a tool in Studio to transform sources into structured outputs — see details in the Studio section below.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Sources Panel
Add source: click the “+” button → choose Upload file or Paste text
Select/deselect sources: tick/untick individual sources to limit answer scope. Newly added sources are automatically selected
View source: click a source name to open the reader, which includes extracted content and the original file (if available)
Delete source: open the “…” menu → Delete source (cannot be undone)
Collapse: the panel can be collapsed into a rail showing source avatars, still clickable to select/deselect
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Chat
### How It Works
The Scholar classifies your questions and responds in the most appropriate way:
| Question Type | Response Method |
| Asking about specific facts/information | Searches sources → answers with citations |
| Asking about notebook overview (“what’s in here?”) | Based on summaries of each source, no search needed |
| Casual conversation (“make it shorter”, “explain again”) | Processes context from the previous answer |
| Asking general knowledge outside sources | Answers with a clear warning that the information is not from your sources |
| Asking when no sources exist | Does not answer, guides you to add documents |

### Chat Features
Source Reader opens when clicking a citation — original passage is highlighted
Clickable citations: each [n] in the answer is clickable to view the original source passage
Follow-up suggestions: 3 suggested questions appear at the end of each answer
Regenerate: click the regenerate button if unsatisfied with an answer
Stop: can stop mid-generation if the answer is too long
Save to notes: save useful answers to the Notes section in Studio
Multiple conversations: create new conversations within the same notebook, each with its own history
### Tips for Effective Questions
Be specific: “Summarize Q2 financial metrics from the annual report” is better than “Summarize”
Select the right sources: deselect irrelevant sources for more focused, faster answers
Use quick suggestions on the start screen to get started
Use the 3 follow-up suggestions after each answer to dig deeper
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Studio — Output Generation Tools
Studio includes 6 tools that transform your sources into structured outputs:
| Tool | Description | Export Format |
| Report | Write a report in 7 preset formats or custom description | Markdown |
| Mind Map | Visualize key ideas as a branch diagram | PNG, SVG, XMind |
| Flashcards | Flip cards to memorize important information | Markdown |
| Quiz | Multiple-choice questions for self-assessment | Markdown |
| Data Table | Extract structured data into comparison tables | CSV |
| Infographic | Generate an infographic summarizing content | PNG |

### Customizing Each Tool
Report:
Report format picker — 7 formats + optional focus field
Choose 1 of 7 formats: Custom description · Report · Key concepts · Action items · Simplified explanation · Study guide · Blog post
Can edit instructions before generating
Add optional focus topic
Mind Map:
Mind map viewer — visual branch diagram, collapsible branches
Number of branches: Condensed (3–4) · Standard (4–6) · Comprehensive (6–8)
Depth levels: Three levels · Four levels
Language
Flashcards / Quiz:
Flashcard viewer — click a card to flip
Quantity: Fewer · Standard · Custom (up to 50)
Difficulty: Easy · Medium · Hard
Infographic:
Infographic modal — choose style, orientation, detail level
11 visual styles (auto, kawaii, clay, sketch note, anime, etc.)
Orientation: Landscape (1536×864) · Portrait (864×1536) · Square (1024×1024)
Detail level: Condensed · Standard · Detailed (beta)
Custom description
Data Table: - Language - Describe the table you want (e.g., “Create a product comparison table by fees, benefits, and conditions”)
### Viewing & Managing Results
Results appear in the Studio list → click to view details
Rename: click “…” → Rename
Download: depends on type — PNG/SVG/XMind for mind maps, CSV for data tables
View recipe & sources: review how the result was created — includes selections, sources read, and instructions
Delete: click “…” → Delete
### Studio Result Detail Views
#### Report — Detail Viewer
Report detail viewer — modal showing structured Markdown report
When clicking a report in the Studio list, a detail modal opens with:
Breadcrumb: Studio › Report — indicates the result type being viewed.
Toolbar (top right):
| Icon | Function |
| ✏️ Edit | Open edit mode for the report content |
| ⬇️ Download | Download the report as a Markdown file |
| 🗑️ Delete | Delete the result from Studio |
| ✕ Close | Close the modal and return to workspace |

Report content: displayed as structured Markdown text — includes headings, paragraphs, data tables, lists, and clearly delineated sections. The report renders directly in the modal, scrolling vertically for long content.
Bottom buttons: - Delete (left): delete the result - Close (right): close the modal
#### Mind Map — Detail Viewer
Mind map detail viewer — branch diagram with export toolbar and zoom
When clicking a mind map in the Studio list, a detail modal opens with:
Breadcrumb: Studio › Mind map
Toolbar (top right): Edit · Download · Delete · Close (same as Report).
Diagram controls (above content):
| Button | Function |
| Collapse | Collapse all child branches |
| ⬇️ PNG | Export diagram as PNG image |
| ⬇️ SVG | Export diagram as SVG vector |
| ⬇️ XMind | Export as XMind file for the XMind app |
| − / + | Zoom out / Zoom in |
| 100% | Shows current zoom level |

Diagram content: displayed as a visual tree: - Root node (red) on the center-left — contains the main topic - Level 1 branches (colored frames) — key ideas - Level 2, 3 branches — details breaking down from parent branches - Each branch has a ⊖ button to collapse/expand child branches - Can pan (drag) and scroll to navigate large diagrams
Bottom buttons: Delete · Close
#### Flashcards — Detail Viewer
Flashcard detail viewer — flip card with Prev/Next navigation
When clicking a flashcard set in the Studio list, a detail modal opens with:
Breadcrumb: Studio › Flashcards
Toolbar (top right): Edit · Download · Delete · Close (same as Report).
Card content: - Displays one large card in the center of the modal with a question (front) or answer (back) - Remaining cards appear blurred on both sides (left/right) creating a carousel effect - Click the card to flip — view the answer on the back
Navigation bar (below cards):
| Element | Function |
| ‹ Prev | Go to previous card |
| 1 / 8 · click a card to flip it | Current card number / total cards + flip instruction |
| Next › | Go to next card |

Bottom buttons: Delete · Close
#### Infographic — Detail Viewer
Infographic detail viewer — AI-generated infographic image
When clicking an infographic in the Studio list, a detail modal opens with:
Breadcrumb: Studio › Infographic
Toolbar (top right): Edit · Download · Delete · Close (same as Report).
Infographic content: - Displays an AI-generated infographic image — summarizes source content into a visual format - The image has a clear layout: numbered steps, illustrative icons, large headings, and brief descriptions for each point - Visual style depends on the choice made during creation (flat, kawaii, clay, sketch note, etc.) - “Generated by AI” watermark in the bottom-right corner - Scrolls vertically if the image is portrait or larger than the modal frame
Bottom buttons: Delete · Close
### Notes
Click Add note in Studio to write free-form notes
Or click Save to notes on a chat answer to save it
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Hub — Overview Page
Hub — notebook grid list with quick stats
The Hub displays: - My notebooks: notebooks you own - Shared with me: notebooks others have shared (read-only) - Continue: return to the most recent notebook - Quick stats: number of sources, notes, conversations
On first visit, you’ll see a 4-step onboarding journey introducing how to use The Scholar: 1. Create a notebook — one notebook per topic 2. Add sources — upload files or paste text 3. Chat — ask questions, get cited answers 4. Generate outputs — transform sources into reports, mind maps, etc.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Language
The Scholar supports Vietnamese and English: - Interface language follows the selection on the TAI Studio toolbar - Chat answers automatically match the language of your question (not the source language) - Studio outputs can have a separate language setting: Follow source / English / Vietnamese
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Tips
Be specific — “Compare Q1 and Q2 revenue in the financial report” yields better results than “Compare numbers”
Select the right sources — deselect irrelevant sources for more focused, faster answers
Use separate notebooks for each topic — sources are completely isolated between notebooks
Combine Chat + Studio — chat to understand documents, then use Studio to create outputs (Studio results will be guided by the current conversation)
Add a notebook description — a general description/context helps overview answers be more accurate
Download results — mind maps export as PNG/SVG/XMind, data tables export as CSV
Save notes — save good answers to notes so information isn’t lost in long conversations
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Limitations
The Scholar only answers based on sources you provide in the notebook — it does not fabricate information
Does not support adding sources via URL/link — you need to upload files or paste content
Right after adding a source, wait a few seconds for indexing to complete before search works fully
Max 20 MB per file; pasted text max 480,000 characters
JSON-based Studio outputs (mind maps, flashcards, quizzes, tables) depend on model output quality — sometimes regeneration is needed
Answers may not always be accurate — always verify important information by clicking citations to read the original source
Does not provide medical, legal, or personal financial advice
⚠️ Please do not upload Sensitive / Confidential / Top Secret documents. Check with the appropriate authority before uploading
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
Last updated: 14/08/2026

# User Guide — The Summarizer
# The Summarizer — User Guide
## Overview
The Summarizer extracts key insights from your documents and produces a concise executive summary with key points. It supports multiple files at once and includes a built-in Vietnamese translation feature.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Supported File Types
- PDF (.pdf)
- Word (.docx)
- PowerPoint (.pptx)
- Plain Text (.txt)
Maximum file size: 20 MB per file
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Interface Layout
The page is divided into 3 panels:
| Panel | Purpose |
| Left (Upload) | Upload files and trigger summarization |
| Middle (Extracted Content) | Shows the raw parsed text from your documents |
| Right (Executive Summary) | Displays the AI-generated summary and key insights |

──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## How to Use
When get to summerize page, the default UI will be
### Step 1: Upload Documents
In the top panel, drag and drop one or more files into the dropzone, or click to browse. You can upload multiple files — each appears as a chip with a remove (×) button.
> ⚠️ PII Notice: Do not upload documents containing sensitive personal information.
### Step 2: Start Summarization
Click "Summarize N file(s)" below. The button shows the count of selected files.
### Step 3: Monitor Progress
Both the middle and right panels show progress indicators:
- Upload — Files are being sent to the server
- Parse — Text is being extracted from documents
- Summarize — AI is analyzing and generating the summary (30–90 seconds)
A progress bar and step indicators show the current phase.
### Step 4: Review Results
Once complete, there are 3 panels with different information:
- Summarize: show comprehensive overview from document context
- Key Insights — Numbered bullet points highlighting the most important findings
- Mind Map - Represent knowledge in uploaded document as knowledge tree
### Step 5: Additional Actions
- Allows display results with both English and Vietnamese
- Store and display the processing history status of documents. This includes the status (Done/Fail) and the detailed summary content, which can be viewed by clicking on the corresponding document.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Tips
- Upload multiple related documents together for a combined summary
- For very large documents, the system uses an advanced multi-pass summarization strategy — a blue info banner will indicate this
- The character count in the middle panel helps you understand how much content was analyzed
- Key Insights are numbered and can be used directly in reports or presentations
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Limitations
- Maximum file size: 20 MB per file
- Very long documents may be truncated due to context window limits
- Summarization typically takes 30–90 seconds depending on document length
- Translation feature translates the summary only, not the full extracted text
──────────────────────────────────────────────────

# User Guide — The Translator
# The Translator — User Guide
## Overview
The Translator lets you upload documents and receive translated versions that preserve original formatting. It supports many file types and languages.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Supported File Types
- PDF (.pdf)
- Word (.docx)
- PowerPoint (.pptx)
- Plain Text (.txt)
Maximum file size: 20 MB
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## How to Use
### Step 1: Select Target Language
At the top, a language bar shows the source language (auto-detected). Use the right dropdown to choose the target language (target language – Vietnamese or English).
### Step 2: Upload Your Document
On the left panel (“Source Document”), drag and drop your file into the dropzone or click to browse. The filename then appears.
> ⚠️ PII Notice: Do not upload documents containing sensitive personal information.
*Note*: Two methods add data—upload a file or input text manually.
### Step 3: Start Translation
For upload file pdf, the interface provides a draggable control for the input document, along with a toggle button group to select the output format (PDF or DOCX).
*Note:* The selected output format is only visible when a PDF file is uploaded; it will not appear for other file types.
Click the "Translate to [Language]" button at the bottom of the left panel. The button enables after a file is selected.
Two languages are currently supported: Vietnamese and English.
### Step 4: Monitor Progress
The right panel (“Translation”) shows real‑time progress:
- Upload — File is being sent to the server
- Translate — AI translates chunk by chunk (progress bar shows percentage and estimated time).
- Build — Final translated file is assembled.
You’ll see: - Current step indicator (Upload → Translate → Build) - Progress bar with percentage - Estimated time remaining (e.g., "Step 3 of 12 · About 2 min left").
### Step 5: Download or Copy Result
Once complete:
- For structured files (PDF, DOCX, PPTX): A download card appears with a "Download ↓" button. The output format matches the input (PDF → DOCX, DOCX → DOCX, PPTX → PPTX).
- For plain text: The translated text appears in the panel with Copy and Download buttons.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Tips
- The translator uses a hybrid LLM strategy: fast model (Haiku) for short content like titles and labels, powerful model (Sonnet) for complex paragraphs. This optimizes speed and quality.
- Translating large documents (50+ pages) may take several minutes; the progress indicator shows real‑time status.
- If a document is too large, it may be truncated — a warning banner will indicate how many characters were translated.
- Cancel a long translation by refreshing the page (the server continues processing but the UI resets).
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Limitations
- Maximum file size: 20 MB
- Supported formats: PDF, DOCX, PPTX, TXT only
- Domain‑specific terminology (legal, medical, financial) may need human review
- PDF output is converted to DOCX format (PDF → DOCX)
- Translation timeout: 10 minutes maximum
- Upon page refresh, the progress information or translated file is no longer visible in the user interface
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
Last updated: 2026-05-25
